title: Remove and Install the In-Vehicle Temperature and Humidity Sensor
introduction:
The small vented panel beside the steering column is the doorway to this sensor. I start with the retaining clips shown in the drawings: the panel comes away first, then the electrical connector and sensor retainers become accessible. Treat the inset like a map of the panel’s little plastic handshake with the dashboard.

The sequence below covers removal and refitting. It does not diagnose a climate-control complaint or establish that the sensor needs replacement.

items.name: Disable remote start
items.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Remove the key
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Eye, ear and hand protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling pointed or sharp-edged parts. Failure to observe these precautions may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Climate-control precautions
items.detail: Review the applicable [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184) before beginning this climate-control repair.

edits.text: Use the Interior Trim Remover at the illustrated edge of the lower instrument panel cover to release its retaining clips. Draw the cover downward as shown and remove it.
edits.why: I use the inset as a clip map: it shows the retainers behind the small vented panel beside the steering column. Removing this cover exposes the sensor mounted on its back.

edits.text: Disconnect the electrical connector. Press the opposed sensor-retaining tabs inward as illustrated, then remove the in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor from the cover.
edits.why: The upper arrow identifies the connector, while the side arrows identify the retaining tabs. Releasing the tabs frees the sensor housing from its mounting.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: refit the sensor into the cover with its retaining tabs engaged, reconnect the electrical connector, then reinstall the lower instrument panel cover and engage its retaining clips.
edits.why: The sensor must be retained in its mounting and electrically connected before the cover closes off access. Check that the sensor and cover are held by their retainers.
